sectiondef.header: Message Flags for AmdXspi_Msg (message-based transfer API)

detaileddescription.para: Not implemented by this core; a running transaction is torn down with SOFT_RESET instead.

description.para: The same bit positions are used by all three registers, but they do not behave alike.

AMD_XSPI_ISR reports each condition as a live level, independently of what AMD_XSPI_IER enables, so it can be polled directly and needs no acknowledgement. AMD_XSPI_INT_EVT latches an event only if the matching IER bit was set when the condition fired, and holds it until it is written back.

The polled paths rely on the live behavior. They test AMD_XSPI_ISR once per message without clearing anything between messages. That is only correct because a bit there tracks the current condition rather than remaining set from an earlier transaction.

briefdescription.para: Every interrupt that reports a fault rather than progress.
RX fill-level events used to drain receive data while a transaction is still in progress, so a read is not limited to one FIFO load.
TX fill-level events used to top the transmit FIFO up while a transaction is still in progress.

detaileddescription.para: So a write is not limited to one FIFO load.

These are the empty-side events, because for the transmit FIFO it is draining that creates the room to write more. This mirrors the RX mask above. Half full is included so the refill starts while the core still has data to clock out. Waiting for empty alone would let it run dry and spend the tCSM budget waiting.

description.para: For xSPI modes only Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0) is supported.
These modes define the data transfer protocol used by the controller.

sectiondef.header: Transmit Register Instruction Format bit definitions

description.para: In Lite mode, the Transmit Register uses a 32-bit instruction format.
User writes instruction first (in 2 AXI-Lite transactions with flags), then command/address/data bytes.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a command/address byte count is valid for the core mode.

detaileddescription.para: The valid counts depend on the mode the core is built in as well as on the field above.

On an xSPI Profile 2.0 core the frame is HyperBus, whose command/address word is always 48 bits, so 6 is the only count the protocol admits. On any other core the count is 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6: one command byte, optionally a command extension byte, and a 3 or 4 byte address. A count of 3, a count of 0 and anything above 6 have no encoding in the field at all. So callers must reject them rather than let them widen to the 6 byte encoding.

parameterdescription.para: SPI mode the core is built in.

simplesect.para: Nonzero if the count is valid, otherwise 0.
C-style signature: u32 AMD_XSPI_IS_VALID_CMD_ADDR_BYTES(u32 Mode, u32 Bytes)

sectiondef.header: IO Format encoding [6:4] for Dual/Quad modes

listitem.para: For Standard modes: always 1-1-1 (do not care).
For xSPI HyperBus: always 8D-8D-8D (do not care).
For xSPI Octal: B3=0 for 8D-8D-8D, B3=1 for 1S-1S-1S.

sectiondef.header: Transmit Register Flag bits (MSB 2 bits of 18-bit FIFO entry)

description.para: The TX FIFO is 18 bits wide with MSB 2 bits as flag bits.

briefdescription.para: Bound on how long either direction waits for the FIFO to become workable: for a read, to report data; for a write, to report room.

detaileddescription.para: The first AMD_XSPI_FIFO_SPIN_COUNT polls run back to back with no delay.

Being slow costs no data in either direction. The core stops the clock when the RX FIFO fills and waits when the TX FIFO runs dry. But it does spend the only budget that matters. Chip select cannot stay low past tCSM, 4 us on this part, and the core raises a transaction error when it does. What the FIFO is waiting on arrives within a clock or two, so the wait must not put a sleep in front of it.

Once those polls are spent, the transaction has outlived its tCSM budget and the core has already failed it. So nothing is gained by continuing to spin, and the remaining polls sleep. That costs the working case nothing. The timeout is then a wall clock bound of about AMD_XSPI_FIFO_SLEEP_COUNT microseconds. It is not a spin count whose real duration depends on the CPU and on AXI latency.

memberdef.definition: typedef void(* AmdXspi_StatusHandler)(void *CallBackRef, u32 StatusEvent, u32 ByteCount)
memberdef.name: AmdXspi_StatusHandler

briefdescription.para: Defines the callback function type for interrupt handlers.

parameterdescription.para: Callback reference passed during handler setup.
Status/event mask that triggered the callback.

briefdescription.para: Holds the configuration entry for each AXI XSPI instance.
Holds the configuration entry for each AXI XSPI instance.
Provides a stub handler for uninitialized callbacks.
Initializes the AXI XSPI driver instance.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if initialization was successful.
XST_DEVICE_IS_STARTED if the instance is already initialized.

briefdescription.para: Aborts the current transfer and returns the core to an idle state.

detaileddescription.para: The core has no abort control, so a software reset is the only way to tear down a transaction that is already running. It is also what the core offers for recovering from a transaction error. The reset also disables every interrupt and discards every latched event, so nothing the abandoned transfer raised is left behind.
The core is enabled again on return, and the clock mode and selected target are put back. So the caller can start a new transfer without any further setup.

briefdescription.para: Performs one or more transfers in polled (blocking) mode.

detaileddescription.para: Each message describes a Lite-mode transaction (command/address plus one data phase). Messages are dispatched to the existing polled engine (AmdXspi_LiteRead / AmdXspi_LiteWrite) in order and the function returns when all messages complete or on the first failure.

parameterdescription.para: Number of messages in the array.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if all messages transferred.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.
XST_FAILURE if a transfer failed.

briefdescription.para: Initiates an interrupt-driven transfer of one or more messages.

detaileddescription.para: This function is non-blocking: it launches the first message and returns immediately. The interrupt handler (AmdXspi_InterruptHandler) drains receive data and advances through the message queue. When all messages complete, it invokes the status handler registered with AmdXspi_SetStatusHandler with XST_SPI_TRANSFER_DONE (or a non-zero error event on failure).

parameterdescription.para: Number of messages in the array.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if the transfer was started.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Serves as the main interrupt handler for the AXI XSPI controller.

detaileddescription.para: This function reads the interrupt status, clears the pending interrupts, and advances the active message queue, reporting the outcome through the handler registered with AmdXspi_SetStatusHandler().
Receive data is drained both on RX fill-level events and at transaction completion. So a read is not limited to what the RX FIFO holds at the end of the transaction.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the AmdXspi instance (cast to void*).

briefdescription.para: Sets the status callback of the message-based AmdXspi_InterruptTransfer().

detaileddescription.para: The handler is invoked from interrupt context with XST_SPI_TRANSFER_DONE when the whole message queue completes. It is invoked with a non-zero error event mask if the transfer fails.

parameterdescription.para: Reference passed back to the handler.

detaileddescription.para: The clock is only programmable in the Standard, Dual and Quad modes. A core built for one of the xSPI profiles runs mode 0 and nothing else, so that is the only value it accepts.

parameterdescription.para:
Clock mode (0-3):
0: CPOL=0, CPHA=0
1: CPOL=0, CPHA=1
2: CPOL=1, CPHA=0
3: CPOL=1, CPHA=1.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_INVALID_PARAM if the mode is out of range, or is not mode 0 on a core built for an xSPI profile.

- XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_INVALID_PARAM if slave number is invalid.

briefdescription.para: Performs a polled SPI transfer (AXI-Lite mode).

parameterdescription.para: Buffer to transmit (can be NULL for read-only).
Buffer for received data (can be NULL for write-only).

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if transfer was successful.
XST_FAILURE if the core reported an error, stalled, or did not signal completion.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is in progress.

briefdescription.para: Looks up the device configuration based on the base address.

simplesect.para:
- A pointer to the configuration table entry if found.
NULL if not found.

briefdescription.para: Polls until the core reports the transaction finished.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS once TXN_COMPLETE is seen.
XST_FAILURE if the core raises TXN_ERROR or the poll expires.

briefdescription.para: Performs a Lite mode read transaction.

detaileddescription.para: This function sends instruction, command/address, and receives data following the Lite mode protocol for xSPI Profile 2.0 (HyperBus).
The receive buffer is taken from the message rather than passed separately, so a caller cannot hand a read the transmit buffer by mistake.
The instance, the message and the ready state are checked by AmdXspi_PolledTransfer(), the only caller. So only the buffers this function goes on to dereference are checked here.

parameterdescription.para: Describes the transaction: command/address bytes, receive buffer, byte count, dummy cycles and frame/IO format.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if failed.

briefdescription.para: Performs a Lite mode write transaction.

detaileddescription.para: This function sends instruction, command/address, and data bytes following the Lite mode protocol for xSPI Profile 2.0 (HyperBus).
The transmit buffer is taken from the message rather than passed separately, so a caller cannot hand a write the receive buffer by mistake.
The instance, the message and the ready state are checked by AmdXspi_PolledTransfer(), the only caller. So only the buffer this function goes on to dereference is checked here.

parameterdescription.para: Describes the transaction: command/address bytes, transmit buffer, byte count, dummy cycles and frame/IO format.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if failed.

briefdescription.para: Starts a single message on the bus.

detaileddescription.para: The message comprises the instruction and command/address, plus transmit data for a write.

This reuses the existing low-level building blocks (AmdXspi_SendInstruction/AmdXspi_SendCmdAddr/AmdXspi_FillTxFifo). It is used both by AmdXspi_InterruptTransfer (to launch the first message) and by AmdXspi_InterruptHandler (to launch each subsequent message on completion).
Nothing here blocks, which is what makes the second of those callers safe.
For a read, the interrupt handler drains receive data as the RX FIFO fills and again at completion. This function only issues the transaction.
The instance, the message and the ready state are checked by both callers. So what is checked here is the message content. Neither of them inspects it, and this function is the first to act on it.

briefdescription.para: Tears down the active message queue and reports the outcome to the caller.

parameterdescription.para: Event to pass to the status handler.
Byte count to pass to the status handler.

detaileddescription.para: The core is left enabled for as long as the instance is ready. So the driver uses this only at initialization, and to restore the core after a register change that requires it to be quiescent.

The core is left disabled, since writing SOFT_RESET returns every control bit to its default. Enabling it is the caller's to do, which for the driver means AmdXspi_CfgInitialize(). Anything the application configured through the option functions is returned to its default and has to be set again.
This can reach past the controller. The core passes the soft reset through to its optional resetn output. So on a design built with that output wired, the attached memory is hardware reset too.

For a HyperRAM, that returns its configuration registers, including the initial latency, to their defaults. It also costs the contents of the array, which the datasheet says to treat as lost. Anything recovering an error through AmdXspi_Abort() inherits that.
Both callers check the instance beforehand. The ready state deliberately is not checked, since AmdXspi_CfgInitialize() resets the core before marking the instance ready.

briefdescription.para: Encodes a command/address byte count into the 2-bit instruction field.

detaileddescription.para: AmdXspi_SendInstruction uses this field.

Callers must screen the count first with AMD_XSPI_IS_VALID_CMD_ADDR_BYTES. It rejects both the counts this field cannot represent and the ones the core's mode does not permit. A count outside 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 that reaches here unchecked widens to the 6 byte encoding. The check is left to callers because they know the mode and can fail the transfer. This function can do neither while returning a field value.

simplesect.para: The encoded 2-bit field value.

briefdescription.para: Assembles an instruction and sends it to the Transmit Register.

detaileddescription.para: The instance and the ready state are checked by the public entry points. The descriptor is a caller local whose command/address field comes from AmdXspi_EncodeCmdAddrBytes, so it is in range by construction. The data byte and dummy cycle counts are checked here. AmdXspi_LiteRead and AmdXspi_LiteWrite pass them straight through from the message without bounding them. So this is the only place the polled path screens them.

briefdescription.para: Sends command and address bytes to the Transmit Register.

detaileddescription.para: Every caller checks the instance, the ready state and the buffer before reaching here, so nothing is rechecked.

parameterdescription.para: Buffer containing command and address bytes.

briefdescription.para: Sends data bytes to the Transmit Register.

detaileddescription.para: Every caller checks the instance and the ready state, and calls this only when the transmit buffer is non-NULL, so nothing is rechecked.

parameterdescription.para: Buffer containing data bytes to transmit.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if all bytes were written to the FIFO.
XST_FAILURE if the FIFO stayed full, which means the core stopped draining it and no error bit was raised to say so.

briefdescription.para: Receives data bytes from the Receive Register.

detaileddescription.para: The payload can be larger than the FIFO, since a Lite read may ask for up to AMD_XSPI_MAX_DATA_BYTES while C_FIFO_DEPTH goes as low as 16 entries. So the data is collected over as many passes as it takes. Each pass waits on RX_EMPTY for data to appear and then drains the number of entries the core reports. That keeps the wait to one register read per poll. It still lets a whole burst be taken without re-testing the FIFO per entry.
A failed transaction is not detected here and is left to run the wait out. So a read that the core has faulted costs the full timeout before it is reported.
AmdXspi_LiteRead(), the only caller, checks the instance, the ready state and the receive buffer, so nothing is rechecked.

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if successful.
XST_FAILURE if failed.

briefdescription.para: Pushes transmit data from the message into the TX FIFO.

detaileddescription.para: Pushes as much data as there is currently room for, without waiting for the core to make more.

Unlike AmdXspi_SendData, this never blocks: it stops as soon as the FIFO is full or the message has been fully written. That makes it safe to call from interrupt context. It also lets a write larger than the FIFO be delivered across successive fill-level interrupts. The write does not have to be pushed in one blocking pass when the transaction is launched.
Progress is accumulated in InstancePtr->MsgTxCnt.

parameterdescription.para: Message whose transmit buffer is being sent.

briefdescription.para: Moves receive data from the RX FIFO into the message buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Progress is accumulated in InstancePtr->MsgRxCnt. So a read larger than the FIFO can be assembled across successive fill-level interrupts. It does not have to be resident all at once when the transaction completes.

WaitForAll says what an empty FIFO means. Part way through a transaction it means the core has not produced the next entry yet, and returning is right. More fill-level interrupts are coming. Blocking in the handler for data the bus has not carried would spend the tCSM budget of the transaction that is still running.

At completion there are no further interrupts to wait for, so the same reading has to be retried. The core signals the transaction complete as the last entries reach the FIFO. The occupancy count crosses into this clock domain a little behind them. So a drain that starts the moment the interrupt arrives can find the FIFO reporting empty with data still landing. Giving up on that first reading loses the tail of the burst and is reported to the caller as a receive overrun.

The retry only ever spins. It runs in interrupt context, and by the time it is reached the bus has already delivered the data. So the wait is the handful of cycles the count takes to catch up, rather than anything bounded by the bus clock.

parameterdescription.para: Message whose receive buffer is being filled.
0 to take only what is present and return, or 1 to wait out a late occupancy count until the message is satisfied.

briefdescription.para: Brings the core to a known state before a transfer is launched.

detaileddescription.para: Any event latched by a previous transfer would otherwise be mistaken for an event belonging to this one. Residue left in either FIFO would be prepended to the payload. Every event is discarded rather than only completion and error. A stale threshold event is just as capable of steering the interrupt handler as a stale completion.

briefdescription.para: Packs an instruction descriptor into the 32-bit instruction word.

simplesect.para: The assembled instruction word.

briefdescription.para: Gets the SPI bus clock (SCK) frequency in MHz.

detaileddescription.para: Config.SpiClkFreq is the clock supplied to the core, which is not what appears on SCK: the core divides it by C_SCK_RATIO. Use this rather than Config.SpiClkFreq wherever bus timing matters, such as working out how long chip select stays low against a device limit.

Returns 0 if the divider is unavailable, which is the case on a BSP generated before this parameter was described in the driver metadata. A 0 means unknown, not zero-frequency, so treat it as "cannot compute".

simplesect.para: SCK frequency in MHz, or 0 if it cannot be determined.
C-style signature: u32 AmdXspi_GetSckFreqMHz(AmdXspi *InstancePtr)

briefdescription.para: Poll bound for a transaction to report complete.

detaileddescription.para: Sized well past the longest Lite mode transfer the core runs so that it only trips on a wedged transaction, never on a slow one.

briefdescription.para: Reads a register value from the AXI XSPI core.

parameterdescription.para: Base address of the AXI XSPI core.
Offset of the register to read.

simplesect.para: The 32-bit value of the register.
C-style signature: u32 AmdXspi_ReadReg(UINTPTR BaseAddress, u32 RegOffset)

briefdescription.para: Writes a value to a register in the AXI XSPI core.

parameterdescription.para: Base address of the AXI XSPI core.
Offset of the register to write.
32-bit value to write to the register.

simplesect.para: C-style signature: void AmdXspi_WriteReg(UINTPTR BaseAddress, u32 RegOffset, u32 Data)
